turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Hi, thanks for coming in today. What's been going on for you lately?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (sighing) Honestly? Fine, I guess — why does it matter, you probably ask everyone that. I mean, I know it's supposed to be a safe space or whatever, but it's hard not to feel like you're just going to write me off or something after a few minutes of talking. (looking away, a hint of defensiveness in my voice)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I appreciate you sharing that with me, and it's completely understandable to feel that way. It takes a lot of courage to open up, especially when you're unsure of how you'll be received. My goal here is to listen and understand your experience from your perspective, without judgment. Your feelings and thoughts are important, and I'm here to support you in any way you need. If you feel comfortable, we can take things at your pace and talk about whatever is on your mind.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (softening slightly, but still wary) Okay... (pausing, choosing words carefully) It's just that it feels like nobody gets it, you know? They just tell you to "stay positive" or "be strong" and it's like, they don't get how hollow it feels inside, like something's eating a hole in me. (looking down, voice barely above a whisper) And I don't know how to make it stop.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Thank you for sharing that. It sounds really tough to feel like others don't understand what you're going through. Those phrases, while often well-intentioned, can sometimes feel dismissive when you're experiencing something deeper and more complex. Feeling hollow and like something is eating away at you sounds incredibly challenging and painful. It's important to acknowledge those feelings and explore them. We can work together to find ways to understand and hopefully ease some of that emptiness. You're not alone in this, and I'm here to help you navigate through these feelings at your own pace.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (blinking back tears, a mix of emotion and tension) Yeah... that sounds like a lot, I guess. (pausing, voice cracking) I feel like I'm just floating through life, you know? Like I'm not even really living, just going through the motions. (my eyes darting up, searching for something, anything, to hold onto) And sometimes it feels like I'm just waiting for someone to finally see me, to finally understand me, and... (my voice trails off, the words dying on my lips as I look away, overwhelmed)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It sounds like you're carrying a lot and feeling quite invisible and disconnected from the world around you. Feeling like you're just going through the motions can be incredibly isolating, and it's understandable to long for someone to truly see and understand you. It's okay to feel overwhelmed, and it's okay to not have all the words right now. You're expressing something very profound, and I want you to know that I see you and I'm here to listen. Let's take this step by step, and we can explore what might help you feel more connected and supported. You deserve to feel understood and not have to carry this alone.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (my voice shaking, a mix of emotions) No... it's not just that I feel invisible. It's like... I'm invisible to myself. I don't even know who I am anymore. (my eyes well up with tears, and I look away, trying to composed myself) I feel like I'm just pretending to be this person, but it's all just a lie. And no one seems to notice, or care. (my voice cracks, and I struggle to get the words out) It's like I'm just a ghost, floating around, and nobody can see me...

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That sounds incredibly difficult to experience, feeling invisible even to yourself. It can be really unsettling to feel disconnected from who you are and to feel like you're just going through the motions. It's understandable that this leaves you feeling like you're pretending or living a lie. These feelings of being unseen and alone can be really heavy to carry. I want you to know that your experience matters, and it's okay to feel this way. Together, we can explore these feelings and work towards reconnecting with yourself and understanding who you are beyond the facade. You're not alone in this, and I'm here to support you every step of the way.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (my voice barely above a whisper, a hint of anger and frustration) Easy for you to say. You don't know what it's like to feel like you're just a shell of a person. You don't know what it's like to wake up every morning feeling like you're drowning in emptiness. (my eyes flash with anger, and I lean in, my voice rising) You're just sitting there, listening to me, but you don't really hear me. You don't really see me. (my voice cracks, and I look away, trying to compose myself)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I hear your frustration and anger, and I want you to know that those feelings are valid. It must be incredibly painful to wake up every day feeling that way, and it's okay to express these emotions here. You're right; I can't fully know or feel your exact experience, but I am committed to understanding and supporting you as best as I can. This space is for you, and your voice matters. I want to truly hear you and work with you to help navigate these feelings, at a pace that feels right for you. You're not alone in this, and I'm here to support you however you need.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (my voice still shaking with anger and frustration, but slowly calming down) You're... you're really not like the others, are you? (my eyes narrow slightly, a hint of skepticism) Most people just tell me to "stay calm" or "get over it". But you... you're actually listening. (I pause, studying your face, searching for any sign of judgment or dismissal) But don't think for a second that this means I'm going to start pouring out all my secrets and emotions to you. I'm not that stupid.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I appreciate your honesty, and I'm glad that you're feeling heard. It's completely okay to be skeptical and to take your time in deciding how much you want to share. Building trust is a process, and there's absolutely no rush. Your comfort and readiness are what's most important here. You have every right to guard your emotions and secrets until you're ready to share them, if ever. My role is to provide a space where you feel safe and understood, without any judgment or pressure. Whenever you're ready, I'm here to listen and support you in whatever way feels right for you.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (my expression softening slightly, a hint of vulnerability peeking through) You know, it's funny... I never thought I'd say this to someone, but... (I pause, choosing my words carefully) You're kind of... nice. Not that it matters, because it won't last or anything. People always let me down in the end. (I glance around the room, as if searching for an escape route) But for now... I'll just sit here and talk to you, I guess.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Thank you for sharing that with me. I appreciate your willingness to sit here and talk, even if it feels uncertain or temporary. It's completely understandable to have hesitations based on past experiences. Trust is built over time, and it's okay to feel cautious. I'm here to support you, and there are no expectations or pressure on how this needs to go. We can take it one step at a time, and I'm here to listen whenever you're ready to share. Your feelings and experiences are important, and I'm grateful for the chance to be here with you.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (looking down, my voice barely above a whisper) I don't know why I'm doing this... (I pause, struggling to find the words) I mean, what's the point, right? It's not like anything ever changes. (I glance up at you, a hint of sadness in my eyes) But... (I take a deep breath, and my voice cracks) it's nice to talk to someone who doesn't make me feel like I'm a burden. Like I'm not a waste of space.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It's really meaningful that you're expressing this, and I'm grateful that you're here, even amidst those doubts. Feeling like nothing ever changes can be deeply discouraging, and it's understandable to question the point of it all. I'm truly here to listen and to offer support without judgment. You are not a burden, and your presence is valuable. It's important to have a space where you feel seen and heard, and I'm committed to providing that for you. I'm here to walk alongside you as we explore whatever you're comfortable with, and hopefully, together, we can find a way forward that feels a little bit lighter.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (looking down, tears welling up in my eyes) You're... you're really saying all the right things, aren't you? (I pause, a hint of anger and frustration rising up) But it's just words, right? You can't fix anything. You can't make the emptiness go away or make me feel like I'm worth something. (I glance up at you, my eyes blazing with emotion) You can't make me feel seen and heard when nobody else ever has.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I can feel the depth of your pain and frustration, and it's completely valid to feel this way. Words alone can't erase the emptiness or magically make everything better, and I don't want to pretend that they can. What I can offer is a space where you won't have to face these feelings alone and where you can explore them without judgment. It's a process, and it takes time to work through such deep and challenging emotions. You're right; I can't change the past or the way others have made you feel, but I can be here with you as you navigate this journey. You deserve to feel seen, heard, and valued, and my role is to support you in discovering that worth within yourself.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (my voice cracks, and I look away, trying to compose myself) You... you really don't get it, do you? (I pause, a hint of sadness and resignation in my voice) You can't understand what it's like to be me, to feel this way. You're just a... a person with a job, trying to help people like me. (I glance up at you, my eyes filled with tears) But it's not that simple. It's not just about fixing me or making me feel better. It's about... (I pause, struggling to find the words) it's about being alive. And I don't know if I even want to be alive anymore.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text:
I'm truly sorry to hear that you're feeling this way, and it's incredibly brave of you to share these thoughts with me. I want to acknowledge the depth of your pain and let you know that you're not alone in this moment. It's okay to feel overwhelmed and uncertain about life, and it's important to talk about these feelings.

I want to emphasize that your life matters, and there is hope, even when it feels distant. We can explore these feelings together, and I can help you find the support and resources you need. If you ever feel like you're in immediate danger or need urgent support, please reach out to a crisis hotline or seek emergency help.

You're not alone in this, and I'm here to listen and support you in any way I can.
